item.title: Fernandes critical of media 'lies' about Carrick relationship
item.description: Bruno Fernandes' penalty sparked Manchester United's second-half revival against Roma [Getty Images] Bruno Fernandes says "a lot of lies" have been reported about his relationship with Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick in recent weeks. Speaking after United's 3-2 win over Roma on Tuesday, it was the first time the 32-year-old had addressed the media since being dropped to the bench after publicly criticising Carrick's tactics in the wake of their 4-1 loss at Como. Restored to the team for the Premier League defeat by Chelsea, captain Fernandes converted a 58th-minute penalty against Roma to spark an improbable second-half comeback from 2-0 down. "It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media," Fernandes told Amazon Prime. "A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air , then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I'm not performing. That's fair. "Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. And, if it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. "It doesn't change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me." Victory against Roma ended a run of nine games without a win, easing some of the pressure on Carrick after a challenging period. But when asked if the result would save his job, Fernandes told Amazon Prime: "We don't need to save anyone's job." He added: "The club needed that win, the players needed that win. We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together." Former Leicester goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel said on BBC Radio 5 Live he liked Fernandes' comments and that he hoped "they can draw a line under all this public stuff and they can get back to winning games". "In Bruno Fernandes' defence is that I've been in football a long time and what's reported in the media is a fraction of the truth usually," said Schmeichel. "The amount of times I saw something written about the clubs I was playing in that couldn't be further from the truth was absolutely staggering. "I hope for Manchester United and Michael Carrick they can draw a line under all this public stuff and they can get back to winning games like they did today." item.title: A half-time speech, a retaken penalty - and a win to save Carrick's job?
item.description: [Getty Images] We cannot know how important Bryan Cristante's foot touching the Roma penalty area as Bruno Fernandes took his initial spot-kick at Old Trafford will prove to be for Michael Carrick. In the moment, as the Roma fans celebrated, and Manchester United trailed 2-0, it seemed catastrophic for the club and terminal for Carrick's position as head coach. But the video assistant referee (VAR) Carlos del Cerro Grande stepped in, advised a retake was required - and at the very least changed the course of the night. Fernandes kept his nerve to drive home his second attempt and then, in a frenzied atmosphere, Matheus Cunha scored twice in the final seven minutes. Even without the context of everything that came before the game, it was the most improbable of comebacks. Even Cunha's sending off soon after, which ensured a nervy ending, would not deny United a first win in 10, bringing some respite after a dreadful few weeks. How did Carrick feel when the penalty was saved? And what did he say at half-time in response to a desperate first-half display that brought condemnation from legendary United figures Wayne Rooney and Nicky Butt, who were covering the game for Amazon Prime? In that moment, there was even a sense of deja vu. "I knew at half-time against Watford," recalled Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in September 2023 of his own dismissal as United boss a couple of years earlier. "At half-time, I told the players it was probably going to be the last time we worked together." United were two goals down at Vicarage Road at half-time that day. Carrick was on the bench as one of Solskjaer's coaches. They went on to lose 4-1. Not this time. "At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated," said Carrick. "The easiest thing is when you keep trying to do something is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That's not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that's the case. We've got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution. "I don't like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what's gone before too much, but it's there. "This place does magical things, it's done it before and it'll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There's just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way. "But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let's have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that." item.title: Emery takes positives, but Villa 'have work to do' to reach Barca level
item.description: Barcelona have won 13 of their 15 games this season after beating Aston Villa [Getty Images] Unai Emery punched the air in frustration at the Spotify Nou Camp. It came from a place of disappointment and exasperation as his Aston Villa side let slip the opportunity of a result in their Champions League tie against Barcelona. They had just fallen 2-0 behind in Spain, having tried to match the hosts blow-for-blow. Raphinha's quick second-half double put the game out of reach after Lamine Yamal's opener, when Villa pressed the self-destruct button just seven minutes in. It could have led to a collapse but, instead, they took the game to the Spanish champions during an engrossing first half, which could - and perhaps should - have yielded a leveller. While defeat ended their 100% Champions League start after three wins, it gave Villa and boss Emery the chance to consider their progress. Barcelona brilliance ends Villa's perfect start Villa firmly believe they belong on this stage. After four years of improvement with Emery they have another chance to prove it. They arrived in Spain with wins against Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, but this was their hardest test. Emery, who celebrated his 55th birthday on Tuesday, wanted to use it as a barometer for their progress, to see how they compared with the current La Liga leaders and five-time European champions. In the driving rain Villa could argue they matched Barca in the opening period and had it not been for Joao Gomes' glaring error that led to Lamine Yamal's strike, and poor finishing, they could have snatched the advantage. Yet they fell short. They have been on the rise under Emery but last season's Europa League winners showed they are still not at the level to win in the Nou Camp. The head coach would also deny it, but perhaps he had something to prove in this stadium which handed him his harshest lesson in the competition nine years ago. In what became known as La Remontada [The Comeback], Barcelona recovered from 4-0 down from the first leg of their last-16 tie to beat Emery's Paris St-Germain side 6-1 in the home return and 6-5 on aggregate. "One more match. Just one more match," said Emery when asked about it on Monday. There was to be no Villa comeback on Tuesday night and Emery's record at the Nou Camp now stands at 15 defeats in 16 games and, in 31 attempts against Barca, he had won just three times. He was able to field what was his strongest available team, but they created their own problems when Gomes' wretched pass gifted Lamine Yamal the crucial opener. Emery, whose side were overtaken by second-placed Barcelona in the league phase table, added: "We are working for years together and we made mistakes like that but we have always overcome those mistakes. I am not blaming him." The self-inflicted wound, though, failed to discourage Villa as they refused to lie down and accept a Barcelona victory. item.title: 'I didn't feel relief!' - Michael Carrick refuses to get carried away as Man Utdend winless run with dramatic Roma comeback
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-MAN UTD-ROMA - AFP Michael Carrick has described Manchester United’s dramatic comeback victory over Roma as an "important night" for the club, though he was quick to downplay suggestions that their season has reached a definitive turning point. The Red Devils overcame a two-goal deficit at Old Trafford to secure a vital 3-2 win, halting a dismal run of ten matches without a victory. Old Trafford witnesses a thriller Manchester United found themselves trailing by two goals against Roma inside 17 minutes on Tuesday evening. The hosts looked destined for another disappointing result before mounting a stunning response to claim a 3-2 victory . The result halted a miserable sequence of three consecutive defeats for the Premier League side. More importantly, it marked their first triumph across their last nine fixtures, injecting some much-needed positivity into a turbulent campaign. Pride takes precedence over relief Despite the immense pressure surrounding his position, Carrick insisted the full-time whistle did not bring him a sense of personal salvation. Instead, the 45-year-old manager focused purely on his squad's resilience and character in overturning the deficit. "Genuinely, no," Carrick responded when asked if he felt relieved. "Whether that's right or wrong, or normal or not, I don't know, but I didn't feel relief. I was genuinely pleased for the players." He praised the effort required to secure the victory, highlighting the determination shown on the pitch. "I could feel their willingness to do well, and so for them to have to dig really deep, and just for everybody, you know," he added. Responsibility and staying grounded The Manchester United boss acknowledged the weight of expectations at Old Trafford, noting how crucial the victory was for collective morale. "I feel the responsibility of that, so to see everybody having that feeling that we all crave. That's why we're all here," Carrick explained. "I really 100 per cent wasn't thinking about myself at that moment - it was just more seeing everybody and the feeling that we can generate when we do things right." While visibly proud of the comeback, Carrick immediately tempered expectations. He refused to label the win a definitive turning point for the club. "I'm not getting too carried away with things," he stated. "I think it's an important night. But we've got to take stock, we've got to stay calm and prepare and be ready for another big game on the weekend." Premier League survival battle United must now attempt to translate this momentum into domestic stability as they return to Premier League action to face Aston Villa before the November international break. Carrick's men currently languish in 17th place in the table , sitting above the relegation zone strictly on goal difference. Securing a positive result against Villa this weekend is essential if the Red Devils are to climb away from the bottom three and begin salvaging their league campaign.

item.title: Gardner-Johnson released by Bills after spitting ban
item.description: CJ Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter [Getty Images] The Buffalo Bills have released safety CJ Gardner-Johnson after he served a one-game suspension for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders' Brock Bowers. The 28-year-old, whose appeal against the decision was rejected, missed week eight's 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. NFL Network reported on Tuesday that the Bills' decision was driven more by inconsistency in Gardner-Johnson's performances than by the spitting incident. Gardner-Johnson started the first six games after joining the team during the off-season. He recorded 26 tackles, two passes defended and one interception for the Bills. Damar Hamlin replaced him in the starting line-up against the Ravens and is likely to retain his place in the team. Gardner-Johnson has also played for the Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens and Chicago Bears since leaving the New Orleans Saints at the end of the 2021 season. item.title: Angel Reese announces return to LSU for exciting appearance after losing the WNBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Atlanta Dream’s Angel Reese is preparing for her first major public appearance since losing Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals, returning to her alma mater. Reese finally delivered on the potential her ardent supporters have said she has in the 2026 WNBA season, leading the Dream to the WNBA Finals in her first season with the team, but losing Game 7 and the title to the Golden State Valkyries. Despite the loss, Reese has cemented her status as one of the best players in the WNBA as the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and the star of a Finals team. Her upcoming plans also highlight her confident attitude. LSU Tigers plan halftime recognition for Angel Reese after WNBA Finals Despite the loss, LSU has announced a halftime recognition ceremony for Reese during their November 5 clash against the Texas Southern Tigers at the Pete Maravich Assembly Center. Reese announced the same on her personal channels with a fitting caption. “The Bayou Barbie is back.” The Tigers will honour Reese after an incredible season in the professional world as a DPOY winner and leading the Dream to the Finals despite not being pre-season favourites. Reese averaged 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals in the regular season and 16.1 points, 11.0 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.7 blocks in the playoffs. Reese won one national championship during her two seasons with the Tigers, famously beating Caitlin Clark’s Iowa Hawkeyes 102-85 in the 2023 NCAA Division I Women’s Tournament Final. This was LSU’s first national championship in Division I women’s basketball. While we have seen certain athletes go away from the media for a while after losing a championship game, Reese is showing that she is willing to bask in the well-deserved appreciation she will get after a career-defining season. As long as the 24-year-old forward is motivated to come back next season and achieve even more, events like this will be frequent at LSU, especially with the shared strong bond between the program and the player. item.title: Retiring Serrano wants to end as a 'game-changer'
item.description: WBO and WBA featherweight champion Amanda Serrano will fight at Coliseo de Puerto Rico for the first time when she faces Skye Falzon [Getty Images] Amanda Serrano said she wants to be remembered as a "game-changer" as she prepares for her farewell fight on home soil next year. Puerto Rico's seven-division world champion will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight titles against Australia's Skye Falzon in San Juan on 9 January. Serrano, who holds a 50-4-1 record with 32 knockouts, previously announced she will retire after the bout , which has been dubbed "The Last Walk" by promoters. "I want people to remember me as a game-changer," Serrano said at a news conference. "I gave it my all in the ring. Every time I fought, every time I trained, I just left everything in the ring, and I hope that you guys see that." Serrano is chasing the women's knockout record, which she jointly shares with American Christy Martin. While Serrano suggested the record would be the "cherry on top", she also wants to make the most of her final appearance in the ring. "I made sure that I went back to the 12 three-minute rounds because I want to enjoy every second, every minute of my last fight in there," the 38-year-old said. "I'm going to go out there and give it my all. If the knockout comes, it comes." Serrano to end career in Puerto Rico in January Serrano draws 3.4m views on TikTok for 50th win Serrano equals knockout record with Hanson victory Falzon, also 38, who holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts, said it was a dream come true to get the chance to fight Serrano. "I actually cried about it," said Falzon. "The opportunity is something I'm going to grab hold of and I just can't wait. "I'm not here just to take part in Amanda's history, I'm here to try to write my own. I wouldn't be a fighter if I didn't believe I could win." Serrano welcomed the confidence from the Australian, saying: "I wouldn't like if any of my opponents would come thinking they're going to come to lose. I love to fight the best out there." Serrano is the first and only Puerto Rican boxer, male or female, to become undisputed world champion, and in 2022 she and Ireland's Katie Taylor became the first female boxers to headline New York's Madison Square Garden. She also defeated Brazil's Danila Ramos in 2023 in the first-ever women's unified world championship contested over 12 three-minute rounds, which is equal to a men's championship fight. Serrano said her decision to retire was simply down to time and she always knew she would hang up her gloves in Puerto Rico. "You guys [have] been with me from the very beginning, supporting me, loving me, and I've been fighting for you guys," added Serrano, who was born in Carolina on the island. "I bring my flag with me, it's in my heart. I'm always with you, and I fight for you. I just want you guys to celebrate my long journey, and it's going to be a great night." item.description: Sir Jim Ratcliffe Manchester United 2024 HIC - Getty Images Manchester United minority owners INEOS have sanctioned a managerial dismissal at FC Lausanne-Sport while debate intensifies over the future of Old Trafford boss Michael Carrick. Sir Jim Ratcliffe's chemical group parted ways with head coach Luka Elsner on Tuesday after just five months in charge of the struggling Swiss outfit. Swiss club dismiss head coach Lausanne-Sport confirmed the exit of 44-year-old tactician Elsner on Tuesday after a dismal start left them rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League table. Appointed on June 1, the manager suffered eight losses across his opening 12 league fixtures while also overseeing two domestic cup ties. His departure arrives shortly after Ratcliffe placed both Lausanne and French club Nice up for sale to streamline his sporting portfolio. Official statement confirms mutual exit Announcing the managerial change via an official club release, Lausanne-Sport stated: "After extensive discussions regarding the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration. "Having taken over as Lausanne's manager on June 1st, Luka Elsner led the first team in 12 Brack Super League matches and two rounds of the Swiss Cup. FC Lausanne-Sport wishes to emphasise the professionalism and commitment that Luka Elsner has demonstrated since his arrival. "He dedicated himself to the club's project with high standards, expertise, and a constant desire to develop his team. His methodological approach and tools also contributed to the development of the coaching staff. "These contributions have enriched the club, which will continue to build upon these achievements. Given that results remain crucial in professional football, the current sporting dynamics have led all parties to agree that ending their collaboration is now the best decision for FC Lausanne-Sport." Old Trafford protests target owners With INEOS scaling back their multi-club operations elsewhere in Europe, the British billionaire's primary footballing focus remains firmly on United, where Carrick's position is under threat following persistent inconsistency that has left them languishing in 17th place in the Premier League. However, supporters are also directing fierce anger at Ratcliffe and the Glazer family as the board weigh up a dugout change. During Tuesday night's Champions League home fixture against Roma, fans in the Stretford End halted play in the 21st minute by throwing green and gold balloons onto the turf while chanting against the owners. At that point, the hosts already trailed 2-0 and were subsequently jeered off at the interval. item.description: Christian Bale opens up about playing Raiders owner Al Davis in ‘Madden’ movie appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the 2026 NFL season in full swing, Las Vegas Raiders fans have an additional treat to look forward to in the form of David O. Russell’s new movie Madden , which features Christian Bale in a supporting role playing the late, great Al Davis . Stopping by SportsCenter to talk about the role with ESPN’s Kevin Negandhi, Bale broke down what it’s like to fill the shoes of such an iconic NFL figure and why Davis is much more complicated than some might think. “Yeah, I mean, the man never backed down from a fight, loved to fight. That was the story that he would say that his dad never let him back down from a fight, ever. He knew every single role within the Raiders. You know, he started as a scout, became assistant coach, coach, he’d been general manager, you know, he was a commissioner and then owner. And he wasn’t somebody with a lot of money who came in and bought the team. He earned his way up to have that team. So we understood everything about it. He was always down on the field,” Bale explained. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He had that motto, you know, once a Raider, always a Raider. And he really stood by it. You know, the man said, ‘All right, to get respect, you’ve got to be feared.’ And I think he liked people to think about him that way. But the people who loved him and knew him very well said he didn’t like to broadcast the fact that he had a really big heart and he genuinely took care of everybody who had been in his inner circle within the Raiders. No matter how many years they’ve been gone, he still took care of them. “And incredible things that he did. You know, he wouldn’t allow the team to play in cities that segregated players. And then on top of that, you know, he had this great civil rights record. He was the first owner to hire an African-American coach in Art Shell, a Latino coach in Tom Flores, and a female executive director in Amy Trask. And they wanted to actually call that the Al Davis rule. And he said, no, no, I don’t want that. Don’t give me that credit. So he was a great contradiction, as all good characters are.” Recalled fondly for his perfectly coiffed hair, need for speed, and iconic “Just win, baby” catchphrase, Davis is a big reason why the NFL is the most popular sport in the United States and continues to grow each and every year globally. While only time will tell how he performs in Russell’s picture, if his track record is of any indication, it’s safe to assume Bale will do a bang-up job stealing every scene he’s in. item.title: Why rugby league needs Tonga-Samoa World Cup final
item.description: Tonga and Samoa met in front of a colourful and fervent crowd in Sydney on Sunday [Getty Images] With blow out wins and a convoluted format, the men's group stage at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup did little to dissuade cynics about the unhealthy state of the international game. From Group A, Australia and New Zealand came through as expected and are widely tipped to face off in the final on 15 November. But from the strange lands of Group B-C, two beacons of hope have emerged. Tonga will face New Zealand after winning all three group matches, before Samoa face Australia in a repeat of the 2022 final. And if either goes all the way, it would be good for international rugby league, shaking up the game in the same way Wakefield's Grand Final win has for the Super League – proving there is still room for surprises in rugby league. "Could this be a dress rehearsal for the final? I hope so," former Bradford Bulls head coach Matthew Elliott told BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra after Tonga and Samoa's riveting Group B-C match, won 20-18 by the Tongans . "I shouldn't say that out loud as an Aussie but I hope so." History suggests this scenario is unlikely, but not impossible. The first semi-final, New Zealand v Tonga, is a match with a dramatic recent history. Tonga beat New Zealand 25-14 in an epic Pacific Championships match two years ago to reach their first-ever elite tournament final. Last year, their meeting was overshadowed by a head injury to Tonga back-rower Eli Katoa, who needed emergency brain surgery after receiving three separate concussions and has not played since. Tonga were semi-finalists in 2017, winning their group after stunning New Zealand 28-22 in the group stage. In the last four they were only narrowly defeated by England, 20-18, scoring three tries in the final seven minutes to give the English a huge fright in their best previous World Cup effort. 'It was an absolute cracker' Tonga and Samoa have met 23 times - both have won 11, with one ending in a draw [Getty Images] Samoa have gone one further of course and were surprise runners-up four years ago having not previously gone beyond the quarter-finals since first appearing at the World Cup in 1995. They were beaten 60-6 by England in their opener but fought through to the semi-finals, where they stunned the hosts 27-26 in a golden point win at Emirates Stadium. At Old Trafford they were overpowered by Australia but not overawed, losing 30-10 . In doing so Samoa became only the sixth different team to reach a men's final after Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain, England and France, in 16 editions. Australia have won 10 of the last 11 World Cups, including the last three, with New Zealand winning the other. Such dominance at the supposed peak of the sport, in a tournament reduced from 16 to 10 teams this year, indicates a gap growing between haves and have nots. item.title: Bayern still in ‘contact’ to sign Man Utd player
item.description: Bayern still in ‘contact’ to sign Man Utd player Bayern Munich are still in contact with wantaway Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel to sign him in the January transfer window. The 16-year-old teenager has expressed his desire to leave Old Trafford, and while Man Utd have not officially terminated his registration, the general expectation is that he will leave at some point in the next year. La Liga giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid are reportedly interested in securing his services, but Bayern are also in the race to sign the prodigiously gifted youngster. JJ Gabriel future: Bayern still in contact (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Christoph Freund has publicly shared his admiration for the youngster, and Bayern are committed to developing players for the future . Christian Falk explained the backdrop of JJ Gabriel’s situation here , and the Bild journalist has further exclusively told CFBayern Insider that the Bavarian giants are still in contact with the player’s camp over a potential move. Bayern are currently struggling with injury problems. Ismael Saibari has undergone surgery for ligament tear, while Serge Gnabry is out for the rest of the year. With Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz also struggling with fitness issues, Bayern could be forced to delve into the transfer market in January. Bayern, in any way, will have to sign a new left winger in the summer, and if they opt to go for a new attacker now, they should go for JJ Gabriel, rather than losing to Madrid or Barcelona in the summer window. Falk says that the move also helps Gabriel, as he can acclimatise for the rest of the season, while he can get playing time due to injuries to other players. Paris Saint-Germain have also been linked, but Bayern are amongst the three top clubs that are heavily interested in signing the youngster. JJ Gabriel: Man Utd career over? (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) The youngster has already requested to leave Old Trafford, although Man Utd have been attempting to resolve their differences with the teenager and his family for the past few weeks. Gabriel joined the Red Devils’ academy at the age of 11 and has proved himself to be one of the most exciting young attackers in world football. He scored 29 goals in 32 appearances for United’s Under-18s before joining the senior squad for pre-season, but has not made his debut. Gabriel’s representatives requested assurances over regular game time, but Man Utd have failed to guarantee that , and as a result, there are strong disagreements over his development pathway. In case, he moves abroad, the Red Devils could receive only a modest training compensation payment rather than a substantial transfer fee.

item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Zach Benson #6 of the Buffalo Sabres controls a rebound in front of Anton Forsberg #31, Quinton Byfield #55 and Brandt Clarke #92 of the Los Angeles Kings with Peyton Krebs #19 during the first period at Crypto.com Arena on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty The Buffalo Sabres got some worrisome news on Monday. In addition to Konsta Helenius being ruled out as week-to-week, Zach Benson missed practice. It wasn’t necessarily an expected absence, and so it raised worries about a potential injury absence for the dynamic winger. Buffalo was returning home from a West Coast trip, and the Sabres are due to host the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday. A Benson absence would make things a bit tougher against a Senators team that has played well in the early going this season. The Sabres got better news on Tuesday, though, and can likely enter Wednesday without feeling too intimidated about what’s going on with Benson. Zach Benson Update The Sabres look set to have Benson available on Wednesday. Head coach Lindy Ruff told reporters Tuesday that after the missed day of practice, Benson returned on Tuesday and looked ready to take part in Wednesday’s clash. It was actually an action-packed Ruff update, shared by Sabres reporter Carson Gates: Lindy Ruff said Zach Benson had a good day and will be available to play tomorrow Said Alex Lyon is “close to being ready.” Conor Timmins didn’t feel good yesterday, but felt much better today. item.title: Cole Palmer third fastest to 50 Premier League goals for Chelsea
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - AUGUST 24: Cole Palmer of Chelsea celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Fulham and Chelsea FC at Craven Cottage on August 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images Cole Palmer reached a bit of a milestone with his successful penalty against Manchester United over the weekend: it was his 50th goal for Chelsea in the Premier League. And yet it was only his 105th appearance in the Premier League for Chelsea! That’s good enough for third fastest all-time , behind both Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink (84 goals) and Diego Costa (85), but just ahead of Didier Drogba, who took one more at 106. Beating Drogba to this mark is especially impressive, though our legendary striker did get off to a slow start in his Chelsea career, and he’s more famous for his big goals on the biggest occasions (a habit that Cole’s also slowly developing ). Palmer’s the eighth player to reach 50 goals for us in the Premier League (Frank Lampard, Eden Hazard, Gianfranco Zola, and Eidur Gudjohnsen also got there, in addition to the three already mentioned), and he’s the 28th player to reach 50 goals in any domestic league competition in our history.
